This device has no NFC reader, so TapPony can\'t scan tags here.
Create a profile first. A profile says where each scan gets sent.
The tag moved away before it was fully read. Hold it still and try again.
This profile needs a tag with NDEF content, and this tag has none.
This tag shows a random ID each time, so its UID can\'t identify it. Use NDEF content or a TapPony launch link instead.
This profile sends plain HTTP to a local address. Turn on \"Allow plain HTTP on the local network\" in the profile to send it.
Plain HTTP only goes to local network addresses. Use https:// for anything on the internet.
That host looks like a number written in an unusual form. Write IP addresses as four plain numbers, like 192.168.1.10.
Put credentials in a header or the auth section, not in the URL.
The URL isn\'t valid. It needs to start with https:// or http:// and the host can\'t contain variables.
The profile uses a secret that isn\'t saved on this device. Add it in Settings.
The JSON body isn\'t valid JSON after filling in the variables.
Header names can only use letters, digits and - _ . characters.
No profiles yet. Tap + to start from a preset.
Allow plain HTTP on the local network
Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can read a plain HTTP request, including any secrets in it.
Only send when the tag has NDEF content
Test sends sample values from a pretend NTAG215, not a real tag.
Saved in Settings. The value never appears in the profile, history or exports.
The scheme and host of the URL must be typed out, not built from variables.

Sent as {device_label} only if a profile uses it. Empty by default, so nothing identifies this phone.
Tokens and keys for {secret:NAME} and the auth helpers. Stored encrypted with a key that stays in the Android Keystore.
TapPony %1$s. Scan a tag, send a request you designed to a server you chose. No account, no cloud, no analytics. Suggested by a tester.
In Home Assistant, create an automation with a Webhook trigger, copy its webhook ID into the URL, and use trigger.json.uid in the actions.
Fires a tag_scanned event with the card\'s UID as tag_id, so an existing badge works as a Home Assistant tag. Save a long-lived access token as the secret HA_TOKEN.
Add an http in node (POST) and put its path in the URL.
Use the production URL of a Webhook node set to POST.
Paste the URL from a Catch Hook trigger.
Paste the URL from a Custom webhook module.
Put your event name in the URL and save your Webhooks key as the secret IFTTT_KEY.
Posts a plain-text notification to an ntfy topic. Pick a topic name nobody will guess, or use your own ntfy server.
Paste a channel webhook URL from the channel\'s Integrations settings.
Paste an incoming webhook URL from your Slack app.
Deploy an Apps Script web app whose doPost appends a row, and paste its /exec URL.
For your own server: a ten-line PHP script that appends each scan to a CSV file. The script is on tappony.app.
Posts the tag details as JSON to any endpoint.
Posts uid, payload and timestamp as a web form.
Sends the UID and time in the query string. Handy for simple logging endpoints.
